hypothesis: Capping glibc malloc arenas can preserve the exact four-worker PrefixGraph candidate/tournament while materially reducing the thread-count-scaled build RSS regression.
conclusion: Allocator arena retention is not the dominant Shifted RSS cause. The best cap saved only about 8.2 percent RSS while costing about 8.3 percent wall time; tighter caps increased observed RSS. Combined with the near-linear 1/2/4 worker RSS frontier, the remaining high-value target is the live memory footprint/ownership of concurrent anchor auditions and their compressed candidate material, not glibc arena tuning.
